title: Integer Euclidean weak Sobolev membership and derivative-sum norm
statement: Over $\mathbf R$ [def-weil-field], use the scalar multi-index derivative, test-function weak-derivative identity and almost-everywhere determined weak derivative of [def-sfb-bundle-sobolev-space]. For integers $m,r,s\geq0$, let $X=\mathbf R^m$ and $Y=\mathbf R^r$, with Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure. Define $f:X\to Y$ to belong to $W^{s,2}$ when $f\in L^2$ and for each multi-index $\alpha$ of total order at most $s$ and each component $k$, there is $d_{\alpha,k}\in L^2$ satisfying $\int d_{\alpha,k}\varphi=(-1)^{|\alpha|}\int f_k\partial^\alpha\varphi$ for every compactly supported smooth real scalar test function. Define $\|f\|_{W^{s,2}}=(\sum_{|\alpha|\leq s}\sum_{k=1}^r\int|d_{\alpha,k}|^2)^{1/2}$, using the existing scalar weak-derivative selection, determined almost everywhere on members. Outside the space the same formula is a total extension. Membership and norms are expressed on representatives of the usual $L^2$ almost-everywhere classes, not by assuming a different norm.

source.place: VI §2, weak Sobolev setup, p.289; supplemental Demailly, Differential and pseudodifferential operators on manifolds, §2, p.3, integer-order description after (2.1), read online https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/analytic_geometry_2019/pseudodiff.pdf.
